fig1_photon_statistics.svg: Photon-number distribution $P(n)$ from photon_distribution() for a coherent state $|\alpha\rangle$ ($\alpha=2$, blue) and a Fock state $|4\rangle$ (orange) of the SAME mean $\langle n\rangle=4$. The coherent bars match the closed-form Poisson $e^{-\langle n\rangle}\langle n\rangle^n/n!$ (circles) with $\Delta n=\sqrt{\langle n\rangle}$ and Mandel $Q=0$ — the 'most classical' light — while the Fock state is a single sharp spike, $\Delta n=0$, $Q=-1$ (sub-Poissonian, nonclassical).
fig2_quadrature_noise.svg: Quadrature variance $\mathrm{Var}\,X=\mathrm{Var}\,P$ from quadrature_variance() vs mean photon number. Coherent states (orange squares) and the vacuum all sit on the minimum-uncertainty floor $\tfrac14$, while Fock states $|n\rangle$ (blue) climb as $\frac{2n+1}{4}$: a perfectly sharp photon number ($\Delta n=0$) is paid for with large, isotropic quadrature (phase) noise — number-phase complementarity. The irreducible $\tfrac14$ is the field's zero-point fluctuation.
